title: Tiny Tweaks
description: Some little tweaks i made for my survival world. Recipe changes, loot table changes, parity changes, subtle world-gen tweaks and more!
body:
Some little tweaks i made for my personal survival world. Recipe changes, loot table changes, parity changes, subtle worldgen tweaks and more! 
Some changes are far too minor to list here. Highly inspired by the [Raspberry Flavored](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/modpacks/raspberry-flavoured) modpack, go check it out !

Changes:

<details>
<summary>Spoiler</summary>

- Allays now can spawn in flower forests, inspired by Raspberry Flavored
- Old growth birch forest trees remodeled (now use the pine tree generator), inspired by Raspberry Flavored
- Slabs can be converted back into full blocks
- Pottery sherds can be duplicated
- Large mushrooms generate in swamps like on bedrock edition
- Implemented the 4 unused paintings (Earth, Water, Fire, Wind)
- Stone tools and other stone recipies can be crafted with any stone type
- Added sunrise and sunset to the /time set command
- Slimes can now spawn in lush caves (although during my testing i didn't see one, but theoretically its possible)
- Added many missing blasting and smoking recipies
- Rotten flesh can be smoked into leather
- Dark oak trees are now taller to make the forests more navigable
- Reworked dye recipes, inspired by Raspberry Flavored
- Ore generation tweaks
- Bats and vexes now spawn in dark forests, inspired by Raspberry Flavored
- Many decorative blocks are now blast resistant
- Strays can drop snow
- Raw ore blocks can be smelted and blasted
- Many more trees will generate with one rooted dirt at their base
- Bread, Shulker boxes, and paper now have shapeless recipies
- Raids can occur in the nether now
- Piglin brutes can drop netherite scrap rarely
- More mobs drop leather
- Plains villages can now generate in meadows and sunflower plains, and taiga villages can now generate in snowy taigas
- More blocks require silk touch
- Suspicious blocks now drop their base block instead of breaking
- Saplings can be crafted into sticks
- Jungle sapling drop rate matches other trees
- Cat gift loot table reworked, inspired by Raspberry Flavored
- Spectral arrows, mushroom blocks, crying obsidian, flint, skulk, nylium, tall grass, tall dry grass, rooted dirt, and cobwebs can now be crafted
- Saplings can be smoked into dead bushes
- Sand and sandstone can be dyed to create their red versions
- Tropical fish spawn in all oceans
- Drowned are more common in dripstone caves
- Husks now drop gold ingots instead of iron ingots
- Shulkers can drop two shells

</details>



Recipe Rebalance:

<details>
<summary>Spoiler</summary>

- Trapdoor crafting now provides 6 trapdoors instead of 2
- Hopper crafting now provides 6 hoppers instead of 1, can also be crafted with a barrel now
- Piston crafting now provides 2 pistons instead of 1
- Stair crafting now provides 6 stairs instead of 4
- Bricks crafting now provides 2 bricks instead of 1
- Nether bricks crafting now provides 2 bricks instead of 1
- Dropper and Dispenser crafting provides 2 instead of 1
- All rail recipes use iron nuggets instead of iron ingots, inspired by Raspberry Flavored
- Rail crafting now provides 12 instead of 16
- Detector rail crafting now provides 8 instead of 6
- Sea lantern crafting now provides 4 instead of 1 
- All torch crafting recipies now provide 6 instead of 1
- Arrow crafting now provides 16 instead of 4
- Bowl crafting now provides 3 instead of 4
- Chain crafting now provides 8 instead of 1
- TNT crafting now provides 8 instead of 1
- Noteblock crafting now provides 4 instead of 1, but requires a copper ingot
- Map crafting now provides 8 instead of 1, and requires black dye instead of a compass
- All lantern crafting recipes now provide 6 lanterns instead of 1, new recipe inspired by Raspberry Flavored
- Candle crafting provides 6 instead of 1
- Item frame crafting now provides 2 instead of 1
- Ladder crafting now provides 6 instead of 3
- Shield recipe is more expensive, new recipe inspired by Raspberry Flavored

</details>
